[EFFECT]
The day of the week has a non-monotonic effect on predicted demand: weekdays (Monday through Friday) produce consistently moderate positive contributions, meaning they reliably boost expected rentals above the baseline. Weekends — both Sunday and Saturday — are highly variable, generating both the largest positive contributions (up to about +0.6 in log terms) and the most negative ones (down to roughly −0.8), meaning some weekend hours see much higher demand than a typical weekday hour, while other weekend hours see sharply lower demand.

[IMPORTANCE]
Weekday is the 4th most important feature out of nine, with an importance score of 0.173. It has a meaningful influence on predicted demand, though hour of the day, temperature, and year are stronger drivers.

[RECOMMENDATION]
Because weekday demand is relatively stable and predictable, you can plan staffing and bike availability for Monday–Friday with confidence; for weekends, however, the wide hour-to-hour swings mean you should plan more flexibly — building in extra capacity for peak leisure hours while avoiding over-stocking during off-peak periods.
